summary: This document describes how a service provider can offer IPv6 VPN service over its packet-switched backbone by extending BGP/MPLS IP VPNs. It defines an IPv6 VPN address family and its route distribution in Multiprotocol BGP, working over IPv4 or IPv6 backbones and tunnels such as MPLS, IP-in-IP, GRE and IPsec.

eli5.summary: A phone company can build private roads for each customer over its shared highways. This extends that idea to customers using the newer, bigger style of internet addresses.

questions: how do ipv6 vpns work over mpls
what is bgp mpls ipv6 vpn
subtitle: How a provider carries customers' private IPv6 networks across its backbone using Multiprotocol BGP and MPLS.

tldr.problem: Service providers already offer BGP/MPLS VPNs for IPv4 customers. They needed the same service for customers whose sites use IPv6, with each VPN keeping its own address space.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a VPN-IPv6 address family: an 8-octet Route Distinguisher plus a 16-octet IPv6 address. PEs advertise labeled VPN-IPv6 routes in Multiprotocol BGP (AFI 2, SAFI 128) and tunnel the traffic over an IPv4 or IPv6 backbone.
tldr.outcome: The IPv6 VPN service looks the same to customers and operators as the IPv4 one, and works over either kind of core. It is a Proposed Standard.

facts.label: Mandatory tunnel type
facts.value: MPLS LSPs set up by LDP

today: RFC 4659 is a Proposed Standard from September 2006. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Reusing BGP/MPLS VPNs for IPv6
sections.content:
RFC 4659 describes how a Service Provider can use its packet-switched backbone to offer Virtual Private Network service to IPv6 customers. It reuses and extends the BGP/MPLS IP VPN method of RFC 4364, and the mechanisms of that RFC apply unless this one says otherwise.

The method uses the same peer model. Customer Edge (CE) routers send their IPv6 routes to the provider's Provider Edge (PE) routers. BGP then carries the routes of a given VPN among the PEs attached to it. CE routers in a VPN do not peer with each other, so there is no overlay visible to the VPN's routing.

A VPN counts as an IPv6 VPN when every site is IPv6 capable and connects natively over an IPv6 interface to a PE. IPv4 and IPv6 handling stay in separate contexts. Communication between an IPv4 host and an IPv6 host, IPv4 VPNs over an IPv6 core, and multicast are all out of scope.
sections.eli5: The phone company already knows how to give each customer a private network. This paper says how to do the same for customers who use the new kind of addresses, without changing how customers see it.

sections.title: The VPN-IPv6 Address Family
sections.content:
A VPN-IPv6 address is a 24-octet quantity. It starts with an 8-octet Route Distinguisher (RD) and ends with a 16-octet IPv6 address. The RD exists only so that distinct routes can be created to a common IPv6 prefix. If two VPNs use the same prefix, the PEs turn them into different VPN-IPv6 prefixes with different RDs, so each VPN gets its own route.

VPN-IPv6 and plain IPv6 addresses belong to different address families, so BGP never treats them as comparable. When a packet's destination is matched in a VRF, only the IPv6 part is matched. The RD format and encoding are those of RFC 4364.

A site that is both IPv4 and IPv6 capable MAY use the same RD for both kinds of address, or a different one for each.
sections.eli5: Imagine two schools that both have a Room 12. Writing the school name in front of the room number tells them apart. The route distinguisher is that school name.

sections.title: Distributing VPN-IPv6 Routes
sections.content:
PEs in the same Autonomous System exchange routes over iBGP, either directly or through route reflectors. For IPv6 VPNs the iBGP connections MAY run over IPv4 or over IPv6. The PEs announce themselves as the BGP Next Hop.

The advertising PE MUST assign and distribute an MPLS label with each route, so it really sends labeled IPv6 VPN routes. They are carried with the BGP Multiprotocol Extensions in MP_REACH NLRI, with AFI set to 2 (IPv6) and SAFI set to 128 (MPLS labeled VPN-IPv6). The NLRI is an 8-octet RD followed by an IPv6 prefix. Route targets work as in RFC 4364.

Two PEs MUST use BGP Capabilities Negotiation (capability code 1, multiprotocol BGP, with the same AFI and SAFI) to confirm they can both process these routes.
sections.eli5: Each router tells its neighbours which private streets it can reach, and attaches a little sticker (a label) so the right traffic can be sorted out when it arrives.

sections.title: Encoding the BGP Next Hop
sections.content:
The Next Hop encoding depends on the speaker's policy: does it want IPv6 VPN traffic tunneled to it over IPv6 or over IPv4? That policy is the network operator's business and is outside the RFC. The RFC warns that a mismatch between the tunneling and the BGP session transport can hide a fault from BGP and lead to black-holing of traffic.

For IPv6 transport, the Next Hop holds a VPN-IPv6 address with an RD of zero and the speaker's global IPv6 address. A link-local address, also with a zero RD, MAY follow it, and only if the speaker shares a common subnet with the peer. The Length field is 24 with only a global address and 48 when a link-local address is included. If peering uses only link-local addresses, the unspecified address stands in for the missing global one.

For IPv4 transport, the Next Hop holds a VPN-IPv6 address with a zero RD whose IPv6 part is an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address containing the speaker's IPv4 address. That IPv4 address must be routable by the other speaker.
sections.eli5: When a router says where to send the mail, it has to write its own address in the right style. Which style depends on whether the delivery trucks use the old or the new kind of roads.

sections.title: Encapsulation and Forwarding
sections.content:
The ingress PE MUST tunnel IPv6 VPN data to the egress PE named by the BGP Next Hop. It looks up the packet's IPv6 destination in the VRF for that CE, finds the VPN-IPv6 route, pushes the route's MPLS label as the bottom label, and then wraps the labeled packet in a tunnel.

If the Next Hop is an IPv4-mapped address, the ingress PE MUST use IPv4 tunneling unless explicitly configured otherwise. If it is not, the PE MUST use IPv6 tunneling. The tunnel can be:

  • MPLS LSPs, where the PE pushes the LSP label directly with no extra IP header.
  • IPv4 or IPv6 tunnels, or GRE, giving MPLS-in-IP or MPLS-in-GRE.
  • L2TPv3, giving MPLS-in-L2TPv3.
  • IPsec-protected tunnels, using IPsec Transport Mode.

For interoperability, every system MUST support tunneling over MPLS LSPs established by LDP.
sections.eli5: The router puts the letter in an inner envelope with a sticker, then puts that inside a bigger envelope addressed to the router at the far end. Only that far router opens the big envelope.

sections.title: Address Types and Multi-AS Backbones
sections.content:
Link-local addresses may be used on the PE-CE link but are never advertised to remote PEs. Global unicast addresses are advertised and handled with no special treatment. Unique Local IPv6 addresses are also supported across sites, but they cannot be used for access to the IPv6 Internet.

When two sites of a VPN sit in different Autonomous Systems, the three approaches of RFC 4364 apply:

  • (a) VRF-to-VRF connections at the border routers, exchanging plain IPv6 routes.
  • (b) EBGP redistribution of labeled VPN-IPv6 routes between neighboring ASes, which needs inter-AS LSPs.
  • (c) Multihop EBGP between PEs in different ASes, with labeled IPv4 or IPv6 routes passed along between ASes. All participating ASes must then use the same kind of tunneling.

Carriers' Carrier service, management VPNs, QoS and scalability follow the considerations of RFC 4364. Multicast is outside the scope.
sections.eli5: Some addresses only work inside one neighbourhood, and some work everywhere. When a private network stretches across several phone companies, they can hand traffic over in three different ways.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The extensions only let MP-BGP carry reachability information for IPv6 VPN routes. The RFC adds no new security machinery. The security considerations of RFC 2545 for carrying IPv6 reachability in BGP apply, and so do the data plane, control plane, and PE and P device security points of RFC 4364.

For IANA, the document uses AFI value 2 with SAFI value 128 for the family "VPN-IPv6 Labeled Addresses". Both values were already in the IANA registries, so IANA need not take any action.
sections.eli5: Nothing new needs locking here. The same safety rules the provider used for the older private networks cover this one too.
